column4: dialect-gated per SUBTEST, NEW with cleat#2059: both tests build their "before" state by applying a SUBSET of the chain (001 alone, or every file but one) and then applying the migration under test on top of it. The rebaseline leaves PostgreSQL three files generated from a pg_dump of the fully-migrated database, so there is no longer a partial chain to build against, and the precondition is gone on PostgreSQL ONLY -- mysql and mssql were not rebaselined and still run their arms. Measured by NAME, not by delta, in this job's configuration (CLEAT_TEST_POSTGRES set, the other two unset): go test ./migration/ -count=1 -json, counting "Action":"skip", reports exactly these two postgres names alongside the four mysql/mssql arms that were already skipping. What is no longer tested on PostgreSQL: that a key written before 010 is re-scoped by 010, and that created_at is backfilled rather than defaulted -- both still covered on the other two dialects.
